page: Amazon Web Services g7e.24xlarge is a graphics-intensive, high-capacity server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) running at 2.4 GHz, supported by a 320 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, the instance integrates four NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 384 GB of VRAM.

Local storage consists of 7600 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 400 Gbps. The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX-TILE, AMX_INT8) for deep learning acceleration, alongside hardware-level cryptography and virtualization flags.

Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier (top 10%) for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, and PassMark CPU encryption. In graphics and AI workloads, it achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench ray tracing, image processing, and LLM inference speed across small, medium, and large models. While stress-ng single-core CPU performance is average, multi-core execution and memory bandwidth remain strong. The combination of high-density DDR5 memory, massive local NVMe storage, and quad workstation-class GPUs offers a resource-dense profile suited for heavy parallel processing without requiring separate storage attachments.

This hardware configuration is optimized for graphics-intensive applications, large-scale LLM inference, real-time ray tracing, high-throughput database operations, and multi-threaded data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services g7e.24xlarge is a graphics-intensive, high-capacity instance designed for demanding parallel computing and visualization workloads. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, it features 96 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8559C processor, 1024.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, and 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPUs with 384 GB of total VRAM, supported by a 400 Gbps baseline network. Benchmarks indicate top-tier performance in LLM inference, ray tracing, image processing, and multi-core CPU operations, though single-core raw compute sits in the average tier. This resource-dense profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for complex workloads by bundling massive memory, high-speed local storage, and quad-GPU acceleration. It is highly suited for large-scale LLM inference, real-time rendering, and data-intensive parallel processing.
